metadata.title: FCE Gap-Fill - 8 Gaps
metadata.description: Open cloze with gap 0 as example. Gaps test grammar across the sentence: auxiliaries, passive, modals, conditionals, reported speech, relatives, linking words, gerunds and infinitives, phrasal verbs, fixed expressions, dependent prepositions, plus the determiners and comparisons the exam also tests. 'area' on each gap names it; a slash lists accepted alternatives.

exercises.title: Lost and Found

exercises.title: The Board-Game Café

exercises.title: The Soup Bus
exercises.text:

exercises.title: Clever Crows
exercises.text:

exercises.title: Postcards for Strangers
exercises.text:

At first nothing happened. Then, about a month later, the replies began to arrive. Some people said thank you, {{3}} others told her long stories about their lives. One elderly man wrote that it was the first message anyone {{4}} sent him since his wife died.

exercises.title: Rain on the Campsite
exercises.text:

By the first evening, everything we owned was soaking. My brother insisted {{2}} cooking dinner on our stove, but the wind kept blowing the flame out, so we ate cold beans from the tin, {{3}} was not quite the feast he had promised.

That night, water came in through a hole in the roof. Neither of us {{4}} sleep, so we sat up talking until dawn. It was the longest conversation we had {{5}} had, and I realised how little I knew him, {{6}} though we had grown up in the same house.

exercises.title: Why Do We Yawn?
exercises.text:
Everybody yawns, but scientists still cannot agree on the reason {{0}} it. For a long time, it {{1}} believed that yawning was the body's way of getting more oxygen. However, experiments have shown that breathing in extra oxygen makes no difference {{2}} how often people yawn.

A more recent theory is that yawning helps to cool the brain, {{3}} works best at a certain temperature. This might explain {{4}} people tend to yawn more in cool weather than on hot summer days.

What is certain is that yawning is catching. Simply seeing someone else yawn, or even reading {{5}} it, can make you do the same. Interestingly, this happens more often between friends and family members than between strangers. Some researchers think this is a sign of empathy, the ability to imagine {{6}} it is like to be someone else.

Dogs can 'catch' yawns from humans, too, but cats, as usual, cannot be bothered. And young children don't start copying yawns {{7}} they are about four years old. So if you {{8}} yawned at least once while reading this, don't worry. It just means you're human.

exercises.title: Chess in the Park
exercises.text:
Every Saturday morning, whatever the weather, a retired postman called Albert Finch sets up two chess boards on a bench in Ashby Park and waits for someone to take him {{0}}. He has done this for nine years, and in all that time he has never once been {{1}} an opponent for long.

exercises.title: The Midnight Visitor
exercises.text:

exercises.title: The Woman Who Mapped the Coast
exercises.text:
